questions.title: Select the Correct Option:
questions.description:
Consider the following C code snippet:

void main() {
  int num[] = {1, 4, 8, 12, 16};
  int *a, *b;
  int i;
  a = num;
  b = num + 2;
  i = *a + 1;
  printf("%d,%d,%d\n", i, *a, *b);
}

What will be the output of the program?
hints: Trace pointer arithmetic: b points 2 elements ahead of a.
questions.editorial: The array num is stored contiguously in memory. Pointer a points to num[0] (*a=1). Pointer b points to num + 2, which is num[2] (*b=8). The variable i is evaluated as i=*a+1=1+1=2. Printing i, *a, and *b produces 2,1,8.

questions.title: Select the Correct Option:
questions.description: Which of the following algorithmic processes relies on a Stack data structure for implementation?

options.text: both recursion and depth first search

hints: Consider which operations use Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) tracking.
questions.editorial: Recursion implicitly uses the system execution stack frame to store function contexts. Depth First Search (DFS) uses a stack (either explicit or via call stack) to backtrack. Breadth First Search (BFS) uses a Queue (FIFO).

questions.title: Select the Correct Option:
questions.description:
Consider the C code below:

#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
  int a = 0, b = 1, c = 2;
  *((a + 1 == 1) ? &b : &a) = a ? b : c;
  printf("%d, %d, %d\n", a, b, c);
  return 0;
}

What values are printed?
hints: Evaluate condition (a + 1 == 1) and the right-hand ternary (a ? b : c).
questions.editorial: Condition a + 1 == 1 evaluates to 0 + 1 == 1 (true), yielding pointer &b on LHS. Right-side condition a ? b : c evaluates to 0 ? 1 : 2 which returns 2. Dereferencing *(&b) = 2 assigns 2 to b. Thus output is 0,2,2.
